pr_title: Avoid undefined behavior of provided macs on EVP_MAC reinitialization
pr_body:
When the context is reinitialized, i.e. the same key should be used
we must properly reinitialize the underlying implementation.
    
However in POLY1305 case it does not make sense as this special MAC
should not reuse keys. We fail with this provided implementation
when reinitialization happens.
    
Fixes #17811

pr_comments: Aargh, we apparently depend on EVP_MAC_init() not failing even for the POLY1305 mac.

Yeah, here: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/801c638c50406c93d683c1ab8bd1d430cff4b6d0/apps/mac.c#L183-L186

The key is passed as a param not via this call.  I prefer the way you are heading but it means an API break :(

I think it can be avoided - done in the fixup.

issue_context.title: Reusing existing HMAC key not possible via EVP_MAC_init()
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/2cc7c9b6981d683711e76c3483f813701b686eb9/providers/implementations/macs/hmac_prov.c#L172-L183

Since the above function does not call `hmac_setkey()` if no key is passed, it does not preserve the semantics of `HMAC_Init_ex()`, which allowed resetting the internal state but reusing the existing key. Is that on purpose?
comments: This truly looks like a bug as the operation (apart from the hmac_set_ctx_params() call) looks like a no-op and that is something I would not expect.

> This truly looks like a bug as the operation (apart from the hmac_set_ctx_params() call) looks like a no-op and that is something I would not expect.

Huh? It's only a no-op if key is NULL.

> Huh? It's only a no-op if key is NULL.

I mean that if key is NULL it's a no-op and successful no-op, which is very surprising, because it actually won't reset the internal `HMAC_CTX *`. This means everything will work fine but the HMAC calculated will be wrong.

If we did not have this possibility to reset the context without setting a key with HMAC_Init_ex() I'd say just keep things as is, however this behavior is useful for performance critical things and it was supported with the HMAC_Init_ex() call.

review_comments: Hmmm. This means the test is going to miss bugs where the initialisation fails when it should succeed. Perhaps we should have a list of algorithms that a re known to fail. If reinit fails for an algorithm that is expected to succeed then the test fails.
Yeah, this is currently the Poly1305 only. I think I can add an option for that.
